# 1 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_012_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Sensing the political moment was right, Jonathan selected envoys and sent them to Rome to reaffirm the alliance that had existed between their nations.

**2** He sent similar letters to Sparta and elsewhere.

**3** The envoys arrived in Rome, entered the Senate, and delivered their message: "Jonathan the high priest and the Jewish people have sent us to renew our friendship and alliance with you, as it was in former times."

**4** The Romans provided them letters of safe conduct to the local authorities along the route to Judea.

**5** The letter Jonathan wrote to Sparta read as follows:

**6** "Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders, the priests, and the whole Jewish people — to their brothers the Spartans, greetings.

**7** Long ago, a letter was sent to our high priest Onias from your king Arius, stating that Spartans and Jews are brothers, both of the family of Abraham. A copy appears below.

**8** Onias received the ambassador with full honors and accepted the letter, which made an explicit declaration of friendship and alliance.

**9** We do not actually need this alliance to sustain us — we have the holy scriptures for that —

**10** but we are reaching out to renew our brotherhood and friendship, because a great deal of time has passed since you last wrote, and we do not wish to become strangers.

**11** We never fail to remember you at every festival and on appointed days — in our sacrifices and in our prayers, as brothers ought to remember brothers.

**12** We are glad to hear of your fame and prosperity.

**13** As for us, we have been through a great deal — surrounded by troubles and wars, with the surrounding kings constantly attacking us.

**14** We did not want to burden you or our other allies and friends with news of these wars,

**15** but we have had Heaven's help, and we have been rescued from our enemies, who have been brought low.

**16** We have chosen Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason to represent us in Rome to renew our old friendship and alliance.

**17** We have instructed them to visit you as well, to bring our greetings and this letter renewing our brotherhood.

**18** Please write back to us."

**19** The text of the ancient letter sent to Onias was:

**20** "Arius king of the Spartans to Onias the high priest, greetings.

**21** A document has come to light establishing that Spartans and Jews are brothers and both descended from Abraham.

**22** Now that we know this, please write and tell us how you are.

**23** For our part, we say: what is yours is ours, and what is ours is yours. We are giving orders that this message be conveyed to you."

**24** Jonathan then got word that the commanders of Demetrius were regrouping with a larger force than before, coming to fight him again.

**25** He marched out of Jerusalem and intercepted them in the region of Hamath, cutting them off before they could set foot on his territory.

**26** He sent reconnaissance teams into their camp; the scouts came back with a report: the enemy was planning a night attack.

**27** At sunset Jonathan ordered the whole camp to stand to arms all night — weapons ready, everyone alert — and he set guards around the perimeter.

**28** When the enemy heard that Jonathan was already in full battle readiness, they panicked. In the night they lit campfires to make it look like they were still there, then slipped away.

**29** Jonathan and his men didn't find out until morning, when they saw the fires still burning with no one there.

**30** Jonathan gave chase but couldn't catch them — they had already crossed the Jordan.

**31** He turned instead and struck the Nabatean tribe called the Zabadeans, killing them and taking their goods.

**32** Then he broke camp, traveled to Damascus, and moved through the entire region.

**33** Meanwhile, Simon marched south to Ashkelon and the neighboring forts, then swung back to Joppa and captured it —

**34** he had received intelligence that Joppa was about to be handed over to Demetrius's forces. He installed a garrison to hold it.

**35** When Jonathan returned to Jerusalem, he called the council of elders together and consulted with them on a program of fortification:

**36** raising the walls of Jerusalem higher, and building a large wall between the citadel and the city — effectively cutting off the citadel, isolating it so its garrison could no longer buy and sell in the city.

**37** Construction began. A section of the eastern wall had already collapsed and was repaired — the section known as Chaphenatha.

**38** Simon built up the town of Adida in the Shephelah, fortified it, and gave it iron gates and bars.

**39** In the background, Trypho was making his move. He was plotting to seize the kingship of Asia, crown himself, and eliminate young Antiochus.

**40** His problem: Jonathan. He feared Jonathan would oppose him and go to war against him. So Trypho needed Jonathan out of the way — dead or captured. He marched to Beth-shan.

**41** Jonathan came out to meet him with forty thousand picked fighting men.

**42** Trypho took one look at that army and froze. He didn't dare move against Jonathan directly.

**43** Instead he welcomed him warmly, praised him before all his officers, gave him gifts, and ordered his whole army to treat Jonathan as they would treat Trypho himself.

**44** Then he said to Jonathan: "Why wear out all these men when there's no war going on?

**45** Send them home. Take just a few escorts and come with me to Ptolemais. I'll hand it over to you — the city, the other remaining strongholds, the troops, the officials, all of it. Then I'll go home. That was the whole point of this trip."

**46** Jonathan believed him. He dismissed his army, and they went back to Judea.

**47** He kept three thousand men — two thousand he stationed in Galilee, and he took one thousand into Ptolemais with him.

**48** The moment Jonathan walked through the gates of Ptolemais, the city's men slammed them shut. They seized Jonathan and cut down every single man who had come with him.

**49** Trypho simultaneously sent his cavalry and infantry north into Galilee and the Great Plain to destroy the rest of Jonathan's forces.

**50** But Jonathan's men there had already heard: Jonathan was taken, Jonathan was dead, all his companions killed. They said nothing. They closed ranks, locked shields, and prepared to sell their lives dearly.

**51** The pursuing force saw men ready to die fighting. They turned around.

**52** The whole Jewish force made it back safely to Judea. They mourned for Jonathan and his companions and they were afraid — deeply afraid. All Israel grieved loudly.

**53** The surrounding nations saw their chance and moved in for the kill: "They have no one to lead them, no one to help them. Now is the time — attack and wipe them out."
